round23_result.summary: 4 of 22 claimed ranges recovered byte-exact. Round 23 concentrated on a byte-regular vtable-setter family, which the round-17 recipe reproduces exactly once the symbol page bias is applied correctly.

0031cd90.mechanism: vtable setter: *(u32*)param_1=&func_0035eb98; func_0023c098(param_1+48); func_002369f0(param_1+24); asm volatile("":::"memory"); *(u32*)param_1=&func_00347f98;

00325aa0.note: both low halves < 0x8000 so no page bias needed

001003b0.reason: empty body: GCC elides the frame entirely for a function with no work; the inline-asm fallback is rejected by this assembler (`illegal operands sd $ra,0($sp)`)

00271828.reason: 2 words: GCC strength-reduces the table index, swapping the sll/addu pair against the lw. v02 (address split) and v03 (<<2 form) both leave the same two words differing

002925c0.reason: 14 words; the callee argument count is wrong (5 guessed), the body is already too long

00295228.reason: 9 words; the frame is 32 not 16 and GCC widens further

002be770.reason: one word short: the target needs `lui t6,0x4000`; a plain 0x4000 literal becomes addiu and the symbol form (u32)(long)&func_00400000 grows the body instead

002ef708.reason: 4 words: the target materialises the two byte-store addresses in two separate registers (t7 and t6, each with its own lui); GCC reuses one. volatile, a memory barrier and named volatile pointers all leave it unchanged

00308018.reason: no source written this round; frame is 144 bytes and arguments arrive shuffled

compiler_level_findings: EMPTY-BODY FRAME (2 members): a function whose body is empty gets no frame at all from GCC 3.2; the target still allocates and saves/restores ra. Not reachable in C, and the inline-asm fallback is rejected by this assembler.

EPILOGUE RESTORE PLACEMENT (3 members, SOLVED this round): the target restores ra between the second lui and the second addiu; GCC emits it after the store. A `asm volatile ("" ::: "memory")` immediately before the final store pins it in the right slot.

corrected_finding.title: The page-bias rule is TWO-CASE, not superseded
corrected_finding.detail: Earlier rounds recorded that the round-15 page bias was an artifact and that the rule is simply truncating (hi == V >> 16). That over-generalised. The high half depends on HOW the symbol is reached: reached by lw/sw it truncates (hi == V >> 16), which is what round 16 001d6538 measured; used as an ADDRESS materialised with lui+addiu the assembler %hi is conservative and rounds (hi == (V + 0x8000) >> 16), which is what round 15 measured. 0031cd90 proved it: symbol 0x36eb98 has low half 0xeb98 >= 0x8000 so the assembler emitted lui 0x37; declaring 0x35eb98 yields the target lui 0x36 + addiu -5224. 00325aa0 needed no adjustment because both its low halves are below 0x8000.

process_notes: Three of this round's misses were my own errors, not compiler behaviour: param_1[0x162] on a u32 parameter (compile error), a v02 "fix" that regressed v01, and the single truncating page rule above.
00271828 sits 2 words from exact across three differently-shaped attempts and is recorded rather than chased further.
